Based on the search results, here's what's happening with the Apple macOS security update in August 2026:

## Critical Screen Sharing Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation

A recently patched security flaw in Apple macOS has come under active exploitation in the wild to deploy a cryptocurrency miner, according to warnings from the Netherlands National Cyber Security Centre.

### The Vulnerability

The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-65400 (CVSS score: 9.8), a critical authentication issue impacting the Screen Sharing component that could allow an attacker already on the network to authenticate to the built-in remote desktop feature service without valid credentials. The shortcoming was addressed as part of an emergency update in macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, and macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 earlier this month.

### Real-World Exploitation

The NCSC has received a notification indicating that active abuse of this vulnerability has been observed on multiple systems on which port 5900 was accessible from the Internet. In all these cases, root had been accessed on the affected system and a Monero crypto miner had been placed.

### Immediate Actions Recommended

Apple fixed it in macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, and macOS Sonoma 14.8.9. Users can update under System Settings > General > Software Update. If immediate patching of the flaw is not possible, it's advised to turn off Screen Sharing by navigating to General > Sharing > Toggle Screen Sharing from "Content & Media."

# Active Exploitation Report for CVE-2026-65400

**Who reported it:**
The Netherlands National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC-NL) issued the warning about active exploitation.

**What they reported:**
The NCSC-NL stated: "In all these cases, root had gained access to the affected system and placed a Monero crypto miner."

**Microsoft's confirmation:**
Microsoft later observed the same pattern, reporting successful root account network sign-ins via Screen Sharing, followed by attackers transferring scripts, SSH keys, and deploying XMRig 6.26.0 cryptocurrency miner.

**Date:**
The article indicates NCSC-NL updated its advisory with exploitation information after August 6, 2026 (when Apple released the patch). Microsoft's observation was shared on August 18, 2026.

**Important note:**
Apple itself did not acknowledge active exploitation in their initial advisory—only that the flaw existed and was patched.

content.content:
# CVE-2026-43760 and CVE-2026-65400 Overview

## CVE-2026-43760
This vulnerability exploits a confused-context condition in macOS Screen Sharing. According to the article, it "exploited a confused-context condition; their write-up ultimately relied on an authenticated session for the conditions to allow the exploit to work." The flaw allows authenticated users via legacy VNC to read and create filesystem artifacts as root.

**Patched versions (July 27, 2026):**
- macOS 26.6
- macOS 15.7.8
- macOS 14.8.8

## CVE-2026-65400
This is the more critical pre-authentication vulnerability affecting Screen Sharing's Secure Remote Password (SRP) implementation. The flaw enables attackers to bypass authentication entirely and execute code as root without credentials. The vulnerability "allows pre-authenticated remote code execution on all supported macOS versions."

**Patched versions (August 6, 2026):**
- macOS 26.6.1
- macOS 15.7.9
- macOS 14.8.9

## Exploitation in the Wild
The document indicates no active wild exploitation is discussed. However, public proof-of-concept code was released by security researchers following disclosure, with the earliest PoC enabling "anyone with the IP address of a Screen Sharing-enabled macOS host" to exploit unpatched systems. The article emphasizes immediate patching is critical for exposed systems.

'y signale **aucune faille activement exploitée**. En revanche, la mise à jour précédente (**26.6.1 / 15.7.9 / 14.8.9**,
6 août 2026) corrige une faille de Screen Sharing dont l'exploitation active a été rapportée — mais **par des tiers, pas par Apple**

.

---

## 1. La mise à jour la plus récente

| Élément | Détail |
|---|---|
| Version | macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 |
| Date | 17 août 2026

|
| Portée | macOS Tahoe uniquement |
| CVE corrigées | ~30 |

- La page « Apple security rele
ases » liste 26.6.2 (17 août 2026) en tête, et indique que « the latest version of macOS is 26.6.2 » ([support.apple.com/

en-us/100100](https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100)).
- Le bulletin détaillé confirme la date et le périmètre,
avec une trentaine de CVE : failles audio (fuite d'informations sensibles), traitement d'images (exécution de code ar

bitraire), trois failles noyau, plusieurs bugs WebKit ([support.apple.com/en-us/148281](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281)).
- **Fait important sur le
périmètre** : Apple n'a **pas** livré d'équivalent pour macOS Sequoia ou Sonoma le 17 août — les Mac incapables de faire tourner
Tahoe n'ont pas reçu cette vague ([macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/08/17/ios-26-6-1-security-fixes/)). Le même jour, Apple a

publié iOS/iPadOS 26.6.1 et iOS/iPadOS 18.7.10.

**Failles activement exploitées identifiées par Apple dans 26.6.2 : aucune.** Le
bulletin ne contient aucune mention de la formule habituelle d'Apple (« Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited… ») ([support.apple.com/en-us/148281](https://support.apple.

rai sujet « exploitation active » : CVE-2026-65400
